answer: When a gale of new signups hits, the network can run a surprise liveness round: every account gets its own puzzle at the same random instant and must answer within seconds. Someone holding a hundred fakes now needs a hundred solvers running in parallel, so cost rises with headcount rather than time. Like a falcon that strikes one target per dive, a lone operator cannot cover many seats at once, and replies draining from one karst of shared servers surface as timing clusters that get discounted.
